hints: Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium: $T\sin\alpha - 4\cos 60^\circ = 0 \implies T\sin\alpha = 2$.
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium: $4\sin 60^\circ - T\cos\alpha - 0.3g = 0 \implies T\cos\alpha = 4\sin 60^\circ - 3$.
Divide the equations to find $\tan\alpha = \frac{2}{4\sin 60^\circ - 3}$, then use Pythagoras or trigonometry to determine $T$.
walkthrough:
Set up horizontal and vertical axes for the particle of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$:
- Ceiling string: exerts a tension of $4\text{ N}$ directed upwards and towards the ceiling at $60^\circ$ above the horizontal.
  Horizontal component: $-4\cos 60^\circ$
  Vertical component: $+4\sin 60^\circ$
- Wall string: attached to the vertical wall at an angle $\alpha$ to the vertical wall, pulling upwards and towards the right.
  Horizontal component: $+T\sin\alpha$
  Vertical component: $-T\cos\alpha$
- Weight of particle: acts vertically downwards: $W = mg = (0.3)(10) = 3\text{ N}$

Apply vertical equilibrium:
$$\sum F_y = 0$$
$$4\sin 60^\circ - T\cos\alpha - mg = 0$$
$$T\cos\alpha = 4\sin 60^\circ - 3$$
Evaluate $4\sin 60^\circ$:
$$4\sin 60^\circ = 4\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 2\sqrt{3} \approx 3.46410\text{ N}$$
$$T\cos\alpha = 3.46410 - 3 = 0.46410\text{ N} \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 1 by Equation 2 to eliminate $T$ and solve for $\alpha$:
$$\frac{T\sin\alpha}{T\cos\alpha} = \frac{2}{0.46410}$$
$$\tan\alpha = 4.309416$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(4.309416) \approx 76.9356^\circ$$
Rounding to 1 decimal place gives $\alpha = 76.9^\circ$.

Solve for tension $T$ using Pythagoras on the two orthogonal components:
$$T^2 = (T\sin\alpha)^2 + (T\cos\alpha)^2 = 2^2 + (0.46410)^2$$
$$T^2 = 4 + 0.21539 = 4.21539$$
$$T = \sqrt{4.21539} \approx 2.05314\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 2.05\text{ N}$.
